pointers.sentence: A Django template is compiled as its `Template` is made: `Template.compile_nodelist` cuts the source into tokens with a `Lexer` and builds the tree of nodes with a `Parser`, which hands a block tag to the compile function registered under its first word (`django/template/base.py:Template.compile_nodelist`).
`Template.__init__` ends by calling `Template.compile_nodelist`, so a `Template` that exists has been compiled (`django/template/base.py:Template.__init__`).

With the engine's `"debug"` option on, `compile_nodelist` uses `DebugLexer`, which also records each token's start and end as `Token.position`; otherwise `Lexer` (`django/template/base.py:Template.compile_nodelist`).
The lexer has one regular expression, `tag_re`, which matches a `{% … %}`, a `{{ … }}` or a `{# … #}` and captures it whole (`django/template/base.py:tag_re`).

`Lexer.tokenize` relies on that order: it flips a flag after every piece, so it knows a tag from text without looking, and passes each non-empty piece to `Lexer.create_token` (`django/template/base.py:Lexer.tokenize`).

`Lexer.create_token` makes a `Token` with a `Token.token_type`, which is `TokenType.TEXT`, `TokenType.VAR`, `TokenType.BLOCK` or `TokenType.COMMENT`; `Token.contents`, the text as written or, for a tag, what lies between its delimiters, stripped; and `Token.lineno`, the line it starts on (`django/template/base.py:Token`).

A block token whose contents are `"verbatim"`, or begin with `"verbatim "`, sets `Lexer.verbatim` to the end tag that will close it, `"endverbatim"` and the same words; until a block token has exactly those contents, every tag becomes a text token holding the tag as written (`django/template/base.py:Lexer.create_token`).
The compile function of `{% verbatim %}` then parses only text, and renders it once into a node that prints the string (`django/template/defaulttags.py:verbatim`).

A compile function usually reads `contents` through `Token.split_contents`, which splits it at white space except inside quotes, and keeps a string marked for translation, `_("…")`, in one piece (`django/template/base.py:Token.split_contents`).

`Parser.__init__` reverses the list of tokens, so that, a comment says, `Parser.next_token`, `Parser.prepend_token` and `Parser.delete_first_token` work at the end of the list in constant time (`django/template/base.py:Parser.__init__`).

`Parser.parse` takes tokens until it meets a block tag whose first word is one of those it was given, or, given no end words, until no tokens are left, and returns the nodes it made as a `NodeList` (`django/template/base.py:Parser.parse`).
`Parser.error` makes a `TemplateSyntaxError` of a message and attaches the token unless the exception has one (`django/template/base.py:Parser.error`).

`Parser.invalid_block_tag` reports a word the table does not hold, with any end words the current parse was waiting for, which is how a misnested end tag shows itself (`django/template/base.py:Parser.invalid_block_tag`).
`Parser.unclosed_block_tag` pops it and names it (`django/template/base.py:Parser.unclosed_block_tag`):

It sets on the node its token and the parser's origin, by which a rendering error finds its line; a comment says why: it cannot change a node's `__init__` (`django/template/base.py:Parser.extend_nodelist`).

A compile function is given the parser and its tag's token and must return a node: `Parser.extend_nodelist` reads `Node.must_be_first` from what it returns and sets two attributes on it, so in practice a `Node` (`django/template/base.py:Node`).
`do_if`, the compile function of `{% if %}`, shows the pattern (`django/template/defaulttags.py:do_if`).

`do_for` checks the shape of `{% for ship in ships %}`, compiles the sequence, and parses to `"empty"` or `"endfor"`; on `"empty"` it parses again to `"endfor"` and drops that token with `delete_first_token` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:do_for`).
`do_extends`, by contrast, parses with no end words, and the rest of the template becomes its node's body (`django/template/loader_tags.py:do_extends`).

`{% with %}`, `{% include %}` and the tags made by `Library.simple_tag`, `Library.simple_block_tag` and `Library.inclusion_tag` read named values with `token_kwargs` (`django/template/base.py:token_kwargs`).

A node that holds others names the attributes that hold them in `Node.child_nodelists`, by default `("nodelist",)`: `TextNode` and `VariableNode` name none, `ForNode` names `"nodelist_loop"` and `"nodelist_empty"`, and `IfNode` answers the default with a property that chains its branches (`django/template/base.py:Node.child_nodelists`).
`Node.get_nodes_by_type` walks the tree through them and returns every node of a class (`django/template/base.py:Node.get_nodes_by_type`).
